{{short description|French physicist}}
'''Pierre Baruch''' (1927–2017) was a French [[Solid-state physics|solid-state]] [[physicist]]. He attended the [[Ecole Normale Supérieure]], and later was on the [[Faculty (division)|faculty]] of [[Paris Diderot University|Universite Paris 7 - Denis Diderot]],

He was awarded the status of [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> after he was nominated by their Forum on International [[Physics]] in 2001<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2001&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2001|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> for his theoretical studies on [[energy conversion]] and the [[thermodynamic]] description of [[photovoltaic cell]] operation, as well as for his numerous actions in support of international scientific cooperation, e.g., through the [[Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development]] and its Megascience Forum.
